knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Carpeted stairs are vacuumed for surface dirt and dust, with the vacuum placed so the cable stays clear. Random vacuuming, wet mopping first, or a leaf blower are not in the procedure.
Hard stairs are swept from the top to the bottom, starting with the edges and corners, and mopped from the top down.
An over-wet or chemical-heavy stair is a slip hazard and can leave a sticky residue when it dries.

practicalCriteria: Learner completes the vacuum pre-use checks on a supplied machine, including the bag, filter, hose, beater bar height and plug, and tags out a planted fault.
Learner sweeps or vacuums a supplied stair section in the correct order, edges and corners first, with the cable kept clear.
Learner mops a supplied hard stair section from the top down and wipes any run marks at once, leaving the surface dry and not sticky.
Learner washes and stores the bucket and cloths, and records the area covered and any gum or damage found.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Vacuum pre-use and end-of-use check record
Assessor observation of the supervised stair clean
Photograph of the finished stair section
stopWorkCriteria: Vacuum fails the pre-use check, or the lead or plug is damaged
Stair is loose, damaged, or unsafe to stand on
Floor is over-wet or sticky and no barrier is in place
Worker is not trained to use electrical equipment
